studios.name: Strawberry Studios
studios.description: This old cinema has been a studio for thirty years and has a lot of tradition. Nowadays, the equipment isn't perfectly up-to-date, but the famous sound is still there.

studios.name: Garage Studio
studios.description: Worn-down, tobacco-smelling underground studio with equipment well past its sell by date. Many rockers get a nostalgic feeling when they hear the name.

labels.name: Rebel Records
labels.description: Small label on a perpetual uphill-struggle. Run by aging enthusiasts.

labels.name: Rainbow Records
labels.description: Small record label that started out as an underground music movement in the seventies. Maybe a bit too nice for their own good.

limitations: Browser playback preserves source cue end boundaries and aligns bar lengths to song tempo. Original per-slice musician jitter and legacy Xtra DSP are not bit-exact.

mission.name: First Steps
mission.intro:
You are in the lower reaches of the music industry, and there are few who believe you can manage a Top 10 hit, stacking the odds up against you completing the Rock Manager journey to fame and fortune found in the upper echelons of the music industry.
   Prove them wrong, get a Top 10 hit!

musicians.name: Glen Jeffries
musicians.description: Bad-mannered, foul-mouthed, hot-tempered punk rocker and wannabe anarchist. Doesn't seem to pay much attention to politics, rather concentrating on cheap beer, bad vodka and two-chord choruses. Lousy on the guitar, but compensates with loads of enthusiasm.

musicians.name: Billy "Alba" Watt
musicians.description: Anarchist punk rocker with wet dreams of the revolution, when the weak will take power. Also an animal-rights-activist and a vegan. Happily fights police, as they represent the oppressing state. Rather a musical talent, skilled at playing both bass and guitar.

musicians.name: Tony "Bubba" McDougall
musicians.description: Small towner who spent most of his adolescence in the garage playing distorted guitar as loud as possible. Moved to Rock City at age fifteen and has played guitar in numerous bands by now. Really skilled at playing the three chords he knows and looks good on stage.

musicians.name: Teddy "Stetson" Helmot
musicians.description: Teddy probably will never win the Nobel prize, but on bass he's as steady as a rock in any band. Prefers the simple to the overly complicated and likes to play it loud. He's content most of the time and likes to party hard. Also a big motor fan.

musicians.name: Corky Jones
musicians.description: Hotheaded lady whose temper has gotten her in trouble more than once. Corky will never be one for tricky rhythm switches, but compensates by beating the drums harder than anyone else. Her arms often cramp, resulting in slower tempo towards the end of the songs.

musicians.name: Sharon Martin
musicians.description: A skilled and experienced vocalist, Sharon had her own band in the eighties and had a few minor hits, but the band never really broke. She's been singing all types of music, but her heart is definitely in straight-forward easy-to-swallow radio rock.

musicians.name: Charlotte Johnson
musicians.description: Decent bass player with star quality and a good stage appearance. Likes to party and is easy to work with most of the time. Very serious about her music, yet hungry for stardom. Perfect for your desktop band  mould her into any form you choose.

musicians.name: Raymond Schneider
musicians.description: Raymond is a semi-celebrity in the gay community after his time as a drummer with Neon Studs in the eighties. The rough years in the lower divisions of show biz has made its marks, and Raymond is prone to powdering his nose a bit too much. At those times, he is a pain to deal with.

musicians.name: Marty Anderson
musicians.description: Matt rides a skateboard and is one of the kindest persons on the planet. He's a vegetarian, a non-smoker, non-drinker, drug-free and likes animals. He's down with the straight edge thing, but thinks it's unnecessary to shout so much.

songs.name: A Love so Smooth
songs.description: This guitar-based pop-rockish love anthem expresses that feeling of romance while rocketing up the charts of any territory.

songs.name: Been Here Before
songs.description: Out-of-the-box, shake your head sideways type pop, just like it has always been played. Fits right in with that eye covering fringe and the smart fishbone suit.

songs.name: Kids Gonna Riot
songs.description: Top-of-the-lungs punk rock where the volume is more important than the message. Hooligan-style sounds that feed on beer and urban despair.

songs.name: Kill Your Parents
songs.description: Powered with all the anger and hate of today's ignored youth, this track is the light that makes schools go up in flames and parents divorce.

songs.name: Sunshine on Lonely Street
songs.description: Don't let the beauty of the song fool you, this is a sad, sad story of solitude and a love lost. This heart is so broken it makes you want to puke.

tutorials.title: Rock City
tutorials.text:
This is Rock City, the unofficial capital of show business.
This is the place for everything you will need to make it: record labels, concert venues, recording studios, song publishers, radio stations, etc.
Start by clicking on the circular icon at the top of the screen to get to the Practice Room.

tutorials.title: Practice Room
tutorials.text:
This moldy and smoke-smelling shack is where your band will be hanging out. Click on the gray boxes to hire musicians for your band.
You can have a minimum of one person to a max of five people in your band. The musicians are paid weekly and their pay demands are stated in the list.
Don't forget to give the band a name (click Change Band Name).

tutorials.title: Song License
tutorials.text:
Now <¤CBand.name> need a demo, but first you have to have a song. Go to a song publisher and purchase the license for a song.
Rock City has two song publishers: the independent Melody Publishing, which is open now, and Global Publishing, part of the powerful Global-concern, which will be available later in the game.

tutorials.title: Recording Studio
tutorials.text:
Time to record – choose a studio and get to it! There are several studios in Rock City, but only two are available at this point – the worn-down Garage Studio and the classic Strawberry Studios.
More will be available later in the game. The more skilled musicians you have, the better the result.

tutorials.title: In the Studio
tutorials.text:
Welcome to the studio. Many a celebrity has spent hours here, smoking and waiting for the engineer to get the gear ready.
Play around with the gears and levers, try out some session musicians, and play around with your track.
When you click OK, the demo is finished and can't be changed.

tutorials.title: Record Label
tutorials.text:
Are you ready to meet the Great White of the music industry – the record labels?
At this point, you can choose between the enthusiasts of Rebel Records or the missionaries of Rainbow Records.
More labels will be available later in the game.

tutorials.title: Concert
tutorials.text:
Do a few live gigs to spawn interest with label execs. Rock City has five concert venues: the suburban Café Lizette, the rough Rock Pit, the elegant Mirror Ball, the classic Avenue and the spacious Palladium.
On top of that is the huge arena Colosseum, but you are far from playing there. Better start with one of the smaller venues.

tutorials.title: Media in Rock City
tutorials.text:
In order to sell records, you'll need some PR. There's a lot of media in Rock City, from Radio FM and TV24 (available later in the game). Both can air your band's songs and videos, do interviews or whatever.
The daily City News prints reviews and entertainment news, just like the music weekly Zer0 Magazine.
There's also the Record Store. Buy adverts and give the reporters gifts to get your band some attention.
Playing live is a good way to get an audience and Rock City has plenty of concert venues so get your hands dirty.

tutorials.title: Design Cover
tutorials.text: You can't release a record without a sleeve. Go to the Design Studio to create a record cover. As usual, the rule is the more money you spend, the better the result.

tutorials.title: Charts
tutorials.text:
There are three charts to top. Radio FM has a list of the most played records every week, TV24 has the Viewers' Chart with the viewers' favourites, and Record Store has a list of this week's top sellers.
Check in to said buildings to contemplate the charts.

tutorials.title: Calendar
tutorials.text:
There's a Calendar to help you plan your strategy, see up-coming events, forecast your financial situation and  see how sales are doing.
Click the date on top of the screen to go to the Calendar.

tutorials.title: Tips on Deals and Demos
tutorials.text: If you have trouble getting a label interested, you might want to try recording a different song or even change your band.

tutorials.title: Request Advance
tutorials.text:
Should you need money, you can ask the label for an advance.
However, they won't give advances without getting something in return. Anything you get, you'll have to pay back in sales.

menuText.title: Please note
menuText.text: When you quit Rock Manager, the game is saved automatically. Next time you can continue where you left off.
